title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word cup? (1 mark)
   A. cupes
   B. cuppies
   C. cups
   D. cup's

2. What does reading for information mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading the page numbers
   B. Reading only for fun
   C. Reading without understanding
   D. Reading to learn something new

3. Vocabulary means (1 mark)
   A. all the words you know and can use
   B. only long words
   C. the pictures in a book
   D. only names

4. Why should you not rush the last lines of a page? (1 mark)
   A. Neatness can be lost when you hurry
   B. The pen will break
   C. It is not allowed
   D. The page will run away

5. A sentence should begin with (1 mark)
   A. a number
   B. a capital letter
   C. a comma
   D. a small drawing

6. What can a weather forecast tell us? (1 mark)
   A. What we will eat
   B. Who will win a race
   C. What the weather will be like
   D. How old we are

7. What is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A story about animals
   B. A list of names
   C. A type of poem
   D. Words that tell someone what to do

8. Which way of reading a sad part is best? (1 mark)
   A. Slowly and softly
   B. Without pausing
   C. Laughing
   D. Fast and loud

9. The word I is always written (1 mark)
   A. as a small letter
   B. in brackets
   C. with a comma
   D. as a capital letter

10. Why do we use punctuation marks? (1 mark)
   A. To hide meaning
   B. To use up ink
   C. To make writing clear
   D. To make pages heavy

11. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. river
   B. road
   C. Nairobi
   D. market

12. What does inferring meaning mean? (1 mark)
   A. Working out meaning from clues
   B. Copying words
   C. Spelling backwards
   D. Ignoring the word

13. What is a cue in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. The last words of the person before you
   C. A drawing
   D. A title

14. What can you use to practise reordering sentences? (1 mark)
   A. Cut strips and arrange them
   B. A bucket
   C. Nothing
   D. A hammer

15. What should you do when you use a simile or metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. Use hurtful comparisons
   B. Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   C. Use very many in one sentence
   D. Never explain it

16. What is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A saying with no comparison
   C. A comparison using like or as
   D. A long story

17. A good ending to an imaginative story usually (1 mark)
   A. repeats the title
   B. starts a new problem always
   C. solves the problem or shows the lesson
   D. has no full stops

18. What does A stitch in time saves nine mean? (1 mark)
   A. Fix small problems early
   B. Nine is a lucky number
   C. Sewing is easy
   D. Stitches are costly

19. What is a good first step when skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the page
   B. Read every word carefully
   C. Close the book
   D. Read the title and headings

20. In The seller counts the money, what is the predicate? (1 mark)
   A. The seller
   B. counts the money
   C. The
   D. money only

21. Which is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   B. A pen
   C. The red pen.
   D. I bought a pen.

22. What is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A title
   B. A sentence with one word
   C. Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   D. A list

23. The goat is inside the shed. Which preposition shows this? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. outside
   C. between
   D. in

24. The cow eats grass next to the river. Which word means the same as next to? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. inside
   C. under
   D. above

25. Which is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Zebra
   C. Cow
   D. Dog

26. How should you read a sad poem? (1 mark)
   A. Without a pause
   B. Fast and loudly
   C. Slowly and softly
   D. Laughing

27. What does intonation add to a poem? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. Extra pages
   C. A new title
   D. The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling

28. Why should you mark pauses in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To know where to stop and breathe
   C. To spoil the page
   D. To hide words

29. What should you do first when studying a picture for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the whole picture
   B. Cover it
   C. Write the ending
   D. Copy a story

30. Which element tells where and when a story happens? (1 mark)
   A. Ending
   B. Title
   C. Setting
   D. Character

31. What is a motion in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. The statement the teams discuss
   B. A song
   C. A dance
   D. A gift

32. How should you read an interjection aloud? (1 mark)
   A. In a flat voice
   B. Very quietly always
   C. With the feeling it shows
   D. Without pausing

33. Which interjection shows surprise? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Ouch
   C. Wow
   D. Shh

34. A good dialogue should have (1 mark)
   A. no characters
   B. only one word
   C. no words
   D. an ending

35. How long should each line in a dialogue usually be? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. Very long speeches
   C. Short, like real speech
   D. One page

36. What should you do before buying a product that an advert says is the best in the world? (1 mark)
   A. Check it and the price
   B. Believe everything
   C. Send money to a stranger
   D. Buy it at once

37. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A time
   B. A thing made or grown for sale
   C. A poem
   D. A place

38. What is a good leader described as in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. Lazy
   B. Rude
   C. Angry
   D. Fair and kind

39. Why should each step contain only one action? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. So it is clear and easy to follow
   C. To confuse readers
   D. To use fewer words

40. What should you do to check if your instructions are clear? (1 mark)
   A. Tear them
   B. Ask someone to follow them
   C. Hide them
   D. Read them backwards

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why sequencing ideas is important in writing. (3 marks)

42. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)

43. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

44. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)

45. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

46. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

47. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

48. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

49. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

50. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)

51. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

52. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

53. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

54. Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural. (5 marks)

55. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

56. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

57. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — cups
   Most English nouns add s to make the plural.

2. D — Reading to learn something new
   We read for information to find facts and learn.

3. A — all the words you know and can use
   Vocabulary is a person's collection of words.

4. A — Neatness can be lost when you hurry
   Careful writing should stay the same to the end.

5. B — a capital letter
   Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

6. C — What the weather will be like
   A forecast predicts the weather.

7. D — Words that tell someone what to do
   An instruction says what to do.

8. A — Slowly and softly
   A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

9. D — as a capital letter
   In English the word I is always a capital.

10. C — To make writing clear
   Punctuation helps readers understand.

11. C — Nairobi
   Names of towns begin with capital letters.

12. A — Working out meaning from clues
   Inferring uses clues in the context.

13. B — The last words of the person before you
   You come in when you hear your cue.

14. A — Cut strips and arrange them
   Strips of sentences can be moved into order.

15. B — Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   Clear and kind comparisons work best.

16. C — A comparison using like or as
   A simile compares two things using like or as.

17. C — solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

18. A — Fix small problems early
   Early action prevents bigger trouble.

19. D — Read the title and headings
   The title tells the topic.

20. B — counts the money
   The predicate tells what the subject does.

21. A — I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   It joins two sentences with so.

22. C — Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   It joins two ideas.

23. D — in
   In shows something is inside.

24. A — beside
   Beside and next to both show the side.

25. B — Zebra
   Zebras live freely on the plains.

26. C — Slowly and softly
   Slow and soft matches sadness.

27. D — The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   Intonation shows meaning.

28. B — To know where to stop and breathe
   Pauses help the listener follow.

29. A — Look at the whole picture
   First see the whole picture.

30. C — Setting
   Setting means place and time.

31. A — The statement the teams discuss
   The motion is the topic.

32. C — With the feeling it shows
   Intonation shows feeling.

33. C — Wow
   Wow is used for surprise.

34. D — an ending
   Every piece needs an ending.

35. C — Short, like real speech
   Real conversations use short turns.

36. A — Check it and the price
   Adverts try to persuade so we check.

37. B — A thing made or grown for sale
   A product is a thing for sale.

38. D — Fair and kind
   The poem advises fairness and kindness.

39. B — So it is clear and easy to follow
   One action per step is clear.

40. B — Ask someone to follow them
   Testing shows whether they work.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader follow the ideas, avoids confusion and makes writing logical.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each valid point.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
   Working / marking points: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.
